question.text: Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>S</mi></math> be the set of all passwords which are six to eight characters long, where each character is either an alphabet from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced open="{" close="}"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>E</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> or a number from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced open="{" close="}"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> with the repetition of characters allowed. If the number of passwords in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>S</mi></math> whose at least one character is a number from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced open="{" close="}"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>6</mn></msup></math>, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math> is equal to

solution.text:
Given total available characters is 10 and total digits are 5,

So, for 6-digit password, the number of ways =106-56

For 7-digit password, the number of ways =107-57

For 8-digit password, the number of ways =108-58

∴  Total ways =106+107+108-56+57+58

=2656+2757+2858-56-57-58

=5626+5·27+25·28-1-5-25=7073·56

Now on comparing with α×56 we get α=7073
